stumbles.quote: Interference colour matches a reference to 0.07 mean ΔE76.
stumbles.why: The post never says what the reference is (a photo, a physical model, a spectral calculation). A mean ΔE76 of 0.07 is also far below what anyone can see, so it reads as a claim I can't judge.

stumbles.quote: checked on a software GPU, not a phone
stumbles.why: The post says the film responds to your phone's tilt, but it was never tested on a phone. I can't tell whether the tilt input works. 'Software GPU' is also unexplained.

stumbles.quote: black film spreads from the top
stumbles.why: 'Black film' isn't explained. A reader who doesn't know soap-film physics won't know it means the very thin film just before it pops. It also isn't clear how this fits with the thick film sinking.
The date only shows how old the build is. It doesn't say what was built or why the date matters, and it could be read as a version marker.

point: It's a WebGPU soap-film simulation that runs in the browser: the film drains with the phone's tilt, thins to black, and pops. Its colours were compared against a reference, but it was only tested on a software GPU and not on a phone.
